title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: I is a 3-element set (I ∈ Ens_3). S_0 T_{0,I} is Grothendieck's discrete Teichmüller groupoid for genus 0 with three marked points (the 'pants' building block of the Teichmüller tower). The previous page gives it explicitly. Its object set is ω(I) = or(I), the 2-element set of orientations (cyclic orders) of I, which is a μ_2-torsor. Morphisms are Hom(x,y) = T_{x−y} ∧_Z Z^I. This is Z^I when x = y and Imp^I (I-tuples of odd integers) when x ≠ y. Composition is addition; parity is additive, so odd+odd lands in even. Equivalently, S_0 T_{0,I} is the Z-groupoid coming from the extension (14), 0→Z→Z→Z/2→0, pushed along the diagonal Z→Z^I. The symmetric group S_I acts on objects through the signature (odd permutations swap the two orientations) and on Z^I by permuting coordinates.

This page computes the fundamental group 'with operators' at an object x. Formula (17): π_1(S_0T_{0,I}, S_I; x) = {(α, l) | α ∈ S_I, l a path between x and αx}. Concretely this is {(α,(n_i)) ∈ S_I × Z^I | all n_i ≡ ε(α) mod 2}, where ε(α) ∈ {0,1} is the parity of α. Formula (18) gives the composition: (l,α)(l',α') = (l∘α(l'), αα') = (l + α(l'), αα'), with α acting on Z^I by permuting indices. The margin note generalises this to paths l: αx → y between arbitrary objects.

The structural argument runs as follows. S_0T_{0,I} is obtained from a Z-groupoid on ω(I) by change of operator group along the diagonal Z→Z^I, and the diagonal is S_I-equivariant. So the canonical extension of S_I by Z^I is the pushout of an extension of S_I by Z. That Z-extension is the π_1 of the principal Z-groupoid with S_I-operators. Its explicit description is the same as (17)-(18), with l ∈ Z and trivial S_I-action. Hence it is the pullback of (14) along sgn: S_I → μ_2, namely {(α,m) ∈ S_I × Z | m ≡ ε(α) mod 2}.

Proposition: π_1(S_0T_{0,I}, S_I; x) is canonically isomorphic to the extension of S_I by Z^I obtained from (14) by pulling back along sgn and pushing out along the diagonal Z→Z^I. The next page adds that this extension is non-split, since its restriction to a transposition gives (14) itself. It splits canonically over the alternating group A_3 (= S_I^+, the stabiliser of x) by α ↦ (0,α).

Interpretation: this is the mapping class group of a pair of pants whose three boundary components may be permuted, measured in half-twist units. Even integers are Dehn twists about the boundaries. An odd permutation acts as a half-rotation, contributing a half-twist (odd entry) at every boundary. This is the basic genus-0 'lego' piece in the program of Esquisse d'un programme.
errors: No substantive mathematical errors. The direction convention for l (x→αx in (17) versus αx→x in the margin) is loose, but (18) is consistent with l ∈ Hom(αx, x) and additive composition.
The parity condition is stated with the signature; as transcribed, the target of sgn is written as F_2 (probably μ_2 or Z/2 in the original). The meaning is the same.

ideas.what: Explicit fundamental group with S_I-operators of the genus-0, 3-point discrete Teichmüller groupoid: {(α,n) ∈ S_3 × Z^3 : n_i ≡ parity(α)}, with composition (l,α)(l',α') = (l+α(l'), αα')
ideas.modern_name: Extended (boundary-permuting) mapping class group of the pair of pants in half-twist units; the 3-holed-sphere piece of the Teichmüller tower / Lego-Teichmüller game
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse, 1984) as programme; worked out by Lochak–Schneps, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps (2000), Bakalov–Kirillov (2000), and Moore–Seiberg in the CFT version
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the genus 0, 3-point and genus 1, 1-point building blocks but gives no explicit computation

ideas.what: Identification of this group as sgn-pullback of 0→Z→Z→Z/2→0 followed by pushout along the diagonal Z→Z^I, using a Z-groupoid with change of operator group
ideas.modern_name: Pullback/pushout of group extensions; groupoids with operators (crossed extensions)

ideas.what: Non-splitting of the extension over S_3, with canonical splitting over A_3 (the stabiliser of an orientation); stated on the next page
ideas.modern_name: Non-split extension of S_3; the half-twist squaring to a full Dehn twist

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but routine explicit computation of the basic genus-0, 3-point building block of Grothendieck's Teichmüller tower. Its content (half-twists, the parity condition, non-splitting over S_3) is well known from Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Bakalov–Kirillov and related work. Only the specific bookkeeping via the or(I) torsor and change of operator groups is idiosyncratic.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'du un point' should read 'en un point x ∈ ω(I)'.
The target of the signature, transcribed 'F_2', is most likely μ_2 (consistent with the previous and next pages: 'l'homomorphisme signature S_I → μ_2').

Likely reading of the middle passage: 'par changement de groupes d'opérateurs abéliens Z → Z^I, le groupe fondamental, extension canonique de S_I par Z^I, peut être regardé aussi comme déduit d'une extension de S_I par Z (savoir le groupe fond. associé au Z-groupoïde (à opérateurs S_I) principal) ... Sa description explicite est la même que (17), (18), sauf que les l sont des éléments de Z au lieu de Z^I — et l'op. de S_I sur Z est triviale. Donc on voit que l'extension canonique n'est autre que l'extension déduite de l'extension (14) de μ_2 par Z, via l'homomorphisme signature S_I → μ_2.'
The condition in (17) reads roughly 'les n_i ont tous la parité définie par sg(α)'.
Margin note likely reads: 'de façon générale, si x, y ∈ ω(I), les flèches de x vers y dans le π_1 ... correspondent aux couples (l,α) avec l : αx → y, avec composition donnée par (18)'.
